notes: Splat Suite 1.21.0 - the render farm now returns work instead of homework. Until now a node pulled the frames out of your clips and solved the alignment, then handed back a camera list pointing at paths on its own disk: you had poses and no photos. A node now builds the DATASET too and sends it home, ready to train in the project's 03_dataset; extract, align and dataset chain on one machine and only the finished article travels. The extracted frames stay on the node - they are the big end and they are reproducible from the clips you still have. Proven on hardware: a 13.1 GB drone clip to another PC, 2,648 images extracted there, one component, 2,645 of 2,648 registered at 99.9 per cent, and 1,639 MB fetched back in 16 seconds at 103 MB/s over gigabit. Also: your .SRT now travels with its clip, so a farm job no longer silently drops the GPS that the same clip keeps when run locally; a node says whether it can finish a job, so an older node keeps working and simply returns the solve; a node's capabilities are asked for rather than remembered, so updating one takes effect immediately; a node never leaves RealityScan waiting for a human, which once held a PC for two hours; a node watches its own export and stops a job that has gone silent for fifteen minutes; and the notice on a busy node puts itself back if anything takes it off screen. A dataset arriving over the network is checked name by name before a byte is written, unpacks beside its destination and moves into place only when complete, and any existing dataset is archived first. Install on EVERY machine - the dataset is built on the node, so a node left on 1.20.0 returns the solve only. One-off: adding the .SRT changes a job's content key, so the first send of a clip after upgrading uploads it once more.
